overview.narrative: Over the last 7 days, 1,713 contacts reached a human. We classify 1,090 (64%) as rightful escalations — exceptions, special-handling, and emotionally hard contacts a bot shouldn't contain. After handoff your team recovered 71% of them; the rest ended worse than they arrived. Recovery is breaking most on special-handling exceptions (like customers traveling with medical equipment) — and three agents recover them far better than the rest.

playbook.intro: These escalation flows are losing the most customers after handoff. Pick one to fix — see who recovers it best, what they actually say, then publish reusable guidance into Agent Assist so every agent gets it.

flows.name: Special-handling exception

examples.quote: Because you travel with medical equipment, I've already arranged a partner-carrier exception and flagged temperature-controlled handling at both airports — set up just for you.
I can see you need special handling — I've personally called ground crew so your equipment is prioritised on and off the aircraft.
I've documented this as a standing exception on your profile, so every future trip is handled this way without you asking.

flows.commonMove: name the special need → personalise it → arrange it proactively (never "it's in the notes")

guidance.template: Because you travel with [special-need], I've arranged a partner-carrier exception on [rebooked-flight] and actioned assistance with [assistance-type] with ground crews at [origin] and [destination] — set up specifically for you.

flows.name: Out-of-policy approval

examples.quote: I've applied a one-time exception and authorised this for you — it's done, you won't need to call back.
This is outside standard policy, so I've personally approved it given your history with us.

flows.commonMove: name the exception as personal and already done — not "let me check if I can"

guidance.template: I've applied a [exception-type] exception and authorised [resolution] for you — it's done. I've noted [account] so this is handled going forward.

flows.commonMove: give a concrete next step + timeline so the wait never feels open-ended

flows.name: High-emotion complaint

examples.quote: That should never have happened, and I'm genuinely sorry it did. I've read through everything — let me fix this properly, not just patch it.

flows.commonMove: validate the emotion explicitly first — name it — then show you read the history before offering any solution

guidance.template: I can hear how [emotion] you are, and that's completely understandable given [situation]. I've reviewed everything — here's exactly what I'm doing: [action], and I'll confirm by [timeframe].

coaching.intro: Each row is an escalation type where your best agents significantly outperform the average — on the same hard contacts. Impact = gap × volume: the bigger the score, the more recoveries are within reach right now.

opportunities.name: Special-handling exception
opportunities.aiSummary: Present a customer traveling with medical equipment whose previous trip went wrong — they're expecting the same failure. The agent must: (1) name the specific equipment need by name, not by category, (2) confirm the exception has been personally arranged — not just 'noted in the system', and (3) proactively close the loop on ground-crew coordination at both airports, unprompted. The failure mode to practice past: reassuring the customer that 'it's in the booking notes' instead of owning the outcome directly.

opportunities.name: Out-of-policy approval
opportunities.aiSummary: Present a customer requesting a fee waiver that sits outside standard policy — they've already been told 'no' once. The agent must make the exception feel personal and already done, not a process the customer is waiting on. Practice point: using 'I've personally approved this' instead of 'I'll need to check whether we can do that'. The failure mode: framing the exception as a favour or escalation instead of an ownership decision.

opportunities.name: High-emotion complaint
opportunities.aiSummary: Present a repeat-contact customer whose frustration has been building across multiple interactions — they've explained the same problem three times. The agent must: (1) explicitly validate the emotion before attempting to solve ('That should never have happened — I understand why you're frustrated'), (2) recap what went wrong to show they read the history, and (3) give a concrete resolution with a named commitment. The failure mode to train past: jumping straight to a solution without acknowledging the emotional state.

opportunities.name: Manager / authority sign-off
opportunities.aiSummary: Present a customer waiting on a discretionary decision that requires manager approval — the outcome is genuinely uncertain. The agent must close the interaction with a definitive answer structure: name who is acting, give a specific next step, and commit to a timeframe — even if the final decision is still pending. The failure mode: leaving the outcome open-ended ('I'll pass it on and someone will be in touch') — the best agents replace uncertainty with a concrete timeline.

opportunities.name: Retention save
opportunities.aiSummary: Present a customer with genuine cancel intent — not a bluff — where a generic retention offer has already failed in a prior contact. The agent must ask one probing question to uncover the root reason before making any offer. Practice point: the offer itself must be personalised to that specific root cause, not a standard discount. Close with a forward commitment that makes staying feel like the obvious choice rather than the path of least resistance.

transcript.text: My flight MSP→CDG was cancelled and I travel with powered medical equipment that needs temperature-controlled handling. I have to get there tomorrow.
I'm sorry — flight VYR221 was cancelled due to the storm. Rebooking onto a partner carrier and the medical-equipment handling both need a specialist to authorize. I'm connecting you to one now.
Okay, I found a seat on EuroAir EA402 tomorrow evening and rebooked you. Anything else?
But what about my medical equipment? Will it actually be handled? Last time it sat on the tarmac and nearly failed. I'm really worried.
It should be fine — it's in the booking notes. You're all set.
That's it? This is exactly what went wrong last time. I need to speak to someone else.

assist.classification: Rightful escalation — partner-carrier + medical-equipment exception. A bot can't authorize this. Goal: recover the relationship.

facts.label: Policy
facts.value: Medical equipment: flag priority offload + temperature-controlled handling with ground services

assist.gap: QM will score Tom's agent skills as usual — but the recovery across this handoff isn't stitched or scored anywhere today. Tom rebooked the flight yet never addressed the equipment, so sentiment never recovered and Alex re-escalated. The best-recoverer move that fixes this isn't in Agent Assist yet.
